# Datamunge

![Datamunge logo](assets/datamunge.png)

Datamunge is a C/C++ library and a template for multi-language bindings.
It uses CMake to build, Just to run development tasks, and a Nix flake to
provide development environments. It is released under the Unlicense.

[Documentation website](https://jordanschupbach.github.io/datamunge/)

```cpp {nix-shell=".#report-cpp", cmd="c++ {file} -o {bin} -std=c++23 $(pkg-config --cflags --libs datamunge) -Wl,-rpath,$(pkg-config --variable=libdir datamunge) && {bin}"}
#include <dm/dm.hpp>

int main() {
  dm::hello();
  return 0;
}
```

```output
Hello datamunge
```

# Test drive

Press C-c C-c inside a block to run it. Each block selects its own Nix shell;
code examples use `report-*` shells, which include the built library or binding.
The first run may build dependencies. Build and REPL commands open a terminal;
exit the REPL or shell to finish that block.

## NixOS

```bash {nix-shell=".#cpp-tools", results="terminal"}
nix develop
```

```bash {nix-shell=".#cpp-tools", results="terminal"}
just build
```

```bash {nix-shell=".#cpp-tools", results="terminal"}
just test
```

```bash {nix-shell=".#cpp-tools", results="terminal"}
just examples
```

```bash {nix-shell=".#cpp-tools", results="terminal"}
just TARGET=datamunge_ex run
```

If Zsh completion mixes Homebrew and Nix versions of `just`, source
`scripts/just-completion.zsh` after `compinit` in your Zsh startup configuration.
It selects the active executable's completion protocol again whenever direnv
changes `PATH`. This prevents newer dynamic completion loaders from executing
an older `just`'s default recipe when you press Tab.

`just build` and `just build-cpp` build the core in Release mode. Standalone CMake builds
also default to Release when no build type is selected; use
`-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` for an explicit debug build. The TensorFlow comparison
uses a separate Release build of both the core and benchmark driver; see
[the comparison workflow](benchmarks/TENSORFLOW.md).
All performance plans and TensorFlow/native comparison tables live in
[PERFORMANCE.md](PERFORMANCE.md).

# Renaming this template

Inspect the rename options below, then run `./rename_datamunge new_project_name`
with your chosen name.

```bash {nix-shell=".#cpp-tools", results="terminal"}
./rename_datamunge --help
```

# Bindings

The [CAD and 3D modelling guide](docs/cad.md) covers `dm::cad` solids, the
ported mep kernel, model formats and offline rendering. The
[Seeed DevArm report](docs/mepml/cad/seeed_devarm.mepml) includes C++/Python/R examples
using the real Seeed DevArm CAD and visual mesh files.

The native CPU game/simulation library and batched physical RL tasks are described
in [the simulation guide](docs/simulation/README.md). GPU compute dispatch is
optional, with native scene import, Courier behaviors and offscreen Vulkan
rendering available. Full NN/GPU physics integration remains in progress.

See [the binding workflow and audit](docs/bindings.md) for source packages, regeneration, and the current language coverage.

### Fortran

Fortran has no REPL: `run-fortran` compiles `examples/fortran/$TARGET.f90` with gfortran
against `build/fortran/prefix` and runs it.

```bash {nix-shell=".#fortran", results="terminal"}
just run-fortran
just test-fortran
```

### Ruby

The Ruby binding is generated by Rosetta: `build-ruby` installs `datamunge.rb` and the native
extension `datamunge/datamunge.so` into `build/ruby/prefix/lib`, and the dev shells put that
directory (and `src/datamungeruby/lib`, whose YARD comments carry the C++ documentation) on
`RUBYLIB`, so `require "datamunge"` works anywhere in the shell. `repl-ruby` is irb with the
binding loaded.

```bash {nix-shell=".#ruby", results="terminal"}
just TARGET=dataframe_ex run-ruby
just repl-ruby
just test-ruby
```

### Octave

The Octave binding is generated by Rosetta: `build-octave` installs the oct-file `__datamunge__.oct`
and the package `+datamunge` (one classdef or function `.m` file per class, enum, function and
constant, committed in `src/datamungeoctave/inst`) into `build/octave/prefix/share/octave/site/m`,
and the dev shells put that directory on the load path, so `datamunge.DataFrame ()` works in
`octave`/`octave-cli` anywhere in the shell. The `.m` files carry the C++ documentation as Octave
help text (`help datamunge.DataFrame.filter`; mep reads it through `MEP_OCTAVE_PATH`).
`repl-octave` is octave-cli with the binding on the path.

```bash {nix-shell=".#octave", results="terminal"}
just TARGET=dataframe_ex run-octave
just repl-octave
just test-octave
```

### Tcl

The Tcl binding is generated by Rosetta: `build-tcl` installs the package directory `datamunge/`
(`pkgIndex.tcl`, `datamunge.tcl` and the stubs extension `datamunge.so`) into `build/tcl/prefix/lib`,
and the dev shells put that directory on `TCLLIBPATH`, so `package require datamunge` works in
`tclsh` anywhere in the shell. Classes are TclOO classes in `::datamunge`. The committed
`src/datamungetcl/pkg/datamunge/datamunge.tcl` carries the C++ documentation as commented
`proc`/`oo::class` stubs (mep reads them through `MEP_TCL_PATH`). `repl-tcl` is tclsh with the
package loaded.

```bash {nix-shell=".#tcl", results="terminal"}
just TARGET=dataframe_ex run-tcl
just repl-tcl
just test-tcl
```

### Guile

The Guile binding is generated by Rosetta: `build-guile` installs the module `datamunge.scm`, its
submodule `datamunge/data.scm` and the extension `libdatamunge_guile.so` together into
`build/guile/prefix/share/guile/site/3.0`, and the dev shells put that directory on
`GUILE_LOAD_PATH`, so `(use-modules (datamunge))` works in `guile` anywhere in the shell. Classes
are GOOPS classes and methods are generics. Every procedure's docstring carries the C++
documentation (`procedure-documentation`, `,describe`; mep reads the committed
`src/datamungeguile/scheme` through `MEP_GUILE_PATH`). `repl-guile` is guile with the module loaded.

```bash {nix-shell=".#guile", results="terminal"}
just TARGET=dataframe_ex run-guile
just repl-guile
just test-guile
```

### Java

The Java binding is generated by Rosetta: `build-java` installs `datamunge.jar` (package `datamunge`,
compiled from the committed sources in `src/datamungejava/java`) and the JNI library
`libdatamunge_java.so` into `build/java/prefix`. The dev shells set `DATAMUNGE_JAVA_LIBRARY` to the
library and `MEP_JAVA_CLASSPATH` to the jar, so `java -cp "$MEP_JAVA_CLASSPATH" App.java` works anywhere
in the shell. Classes are `AutoCloseable`, module functions are static methods of `datamunge.Datamunge`
and the datasets are in `datamunge.data.Data`. The generated sources carry the C++ documentation as
Javadoc (mep reads them through `MEP_JAVA_SOURCEPATH`). `repl-java` is jshell with the jar on the class
path and `import datamunge.*;` done.

```bash {nix-shell=".#java", results="terminal"}
just TARGET=dataframe_ex run-java
just repl-java
just test-java
```

### Go

The Go binding is generated by Rosetta: `build-go` installs the shared library `libdatamunge_go.so`
into `build/go/prefix/lib`, and the committed module `src/datamungego/go/datamunge` (package
`datamunge`, plus `datamunge/data` for the datasets) calls it through cgo. The dev shells set
`CGO_LDFLAGS` to that directory (with an rpath) and `GOWORK` to `build/go/go.work`, a workspace with
the module, `examples/go` and `tests/go`, so `go run examples/go/x.go` works from the root and a Go
program anywhere in the shell can `import "datamunge"`. Elsewhere, `require datamunge v0.0.0` and
`replace datamunge => <path>/src/datamungego/go/datamunge` in go.mod (as `examples/go/go.mod` does).
Calls return `(T, error)`, constructors are `NewX`, overloads and C++ defaults are named variants
(`SortBy`, `SortByWithAscending`), and `Close` frees an object. The module carries the C++
documentation as godoc comments (`go doc datamunge.Seql`; mep reads them through the go.mod
`replace`). Go has no REPL, so there is no `repl-go`.

```bash {nix-shell=".#go", results="terminal"}
just TARGET=dataframe_ex run-go
just test-go
```

### OCaml

The OCaml binding is generated by Rosetta: `build-ocaml` installs the findlib package `datamunge`
(`META`, `datamunge.cma`/`.cmxa`, the C++ stubs `dlldatamunge_stubs.so` and `libdatamunge_stubs.a`)
into `build/ocaml/prefix/lib`, compiled from the committed `src/datamungeocaml/ocaml/datamunge`. The
dev shells put that directory on `OCAMLPATH`, so `ocamlfind ocamlopt -package datamunge -linkpkg x.ml`,
dune `(libraries datamunge)` and `#require "datamunge"` in the toplevel work anywhere in the shell
(native programs link `libdatamunge` with an rpath). Classes are submodules (`DataFrame`, `LM`) whose
functions take the object first, C++ defaults are optional labelled arguments, overloads are
type-suffixed functions, and OCaml subclasses override virtual methods through `extend`. The
committed `datamunge.mli` carries the C++ documentation as odoc comments (mep reads it through
`MEP_OCAML_PATH`). `repl-ocaml` is utop with the package loaded and opened.

```bash {nix-shell=".#ocaml", results="terminal"}
just TARGET=dataframe_ex run-ocaml
just repl-ocaml
just test-ocaml
```

## Binding coverage

| Language    | Name                | Implemented |
|-------------|---------------------|-------------|
| APL (GNU)   | Datamunge (Rosetta) | ✅           |
| C\#         | Datamunge (Rosetta) | ✅           |
| Common Lisp | datamunge (Rosetta) | ✅           |
| D           | DDatamunge          | ✅           |
| Fortran     | datamunge (Rosetta) | ✅           |
| Go          | Datamunge (Rosetta) | ✅           |
| Guile       | datamunge (Rosetta) | ✅           |
| Java        | Datamunge (Rosetta) | ✅           |
| Julia       | Datamunge (Rosetta) | ✅           |
| Javascript  | DatamungeJS         | ✅           |
| Lua         | Ldatamunge          | ✅           |
| OCaml       | Datamunge (Rosetta) | ✅           |
| Octave      | datamunge (Rosetta) | ✅           |
| PHP         | DatamungePHP        | ✅           |
| Perl        | Pdatamunge          | ✅           |
| Python      | PyDatamunge         | ✅           |
| R           | DatamungeR          | ✅           |
| Ruby        | Datamunge (Rosetta) | ✅           |
| Rust        | RustDatamunge       | ✅           |
| Tcl         | Datamunge (Rosetta) | ✅           |

Each binding lives under `src/` (e.g. `src/rustdatamunge/`, `src/datamungego/`, `src/datamungeguile/`),
with SWIG generator inputs kept alongside each binding (typically `src/<binding>/swig/`).
The APL, C\#, Common Lisp, Fortran, Go, Java, Julia, OCaml, Octave, Ruby and Tcl bindings are generated by Rosetta instead, from the
Clang AST (`src/datamunge<lang>/rosetta/`); their docstrings (`⍝` comments in the APL script, XML doc comments in C\#,
FORD `!>` comments in Fortran, godoc comments in Go, Javadoc in Java, `.m` help text in Octave, YARD comments in Ruby, commented `proc`/`oo::class`
stubs in Tcl) come from the
Doxygen comments.
The tensor/NN facade is currently exposed in Python and R; the other bindings
cover their existing core APIs. The C/C++ core remains the single
source of truth; bindings are (re)generated via the `just prebuild-*` /
`just build-*` workflows.

CNN and autoencoder examples (sections 1 and 2) are available in
[C++](examples/cpp/source/nn/README.md) and through [Python/SWIG](examples/python/nn/README.md).

The NN language rewrite covers 414 canonical C++ examples across foundations,
CNNs, autoencoders, generative models, recurrent networks, attention and RL.
Actual implementations use the functional SWIG API (`pydatamunge.nn` /
`datamungerNN::nn`) with models and loops written in each language. Track completed
ports and validation in [the migration ledger](prebindings/nn/language_status.json)
with `just nn-language-status`; compiled reference wrappers do not count as ports.

Run a completed port with `just python-example NAME epochs=5` or
`just r-example NAME epochs=5`. Both commands reject unported examples; use
`just run-nn NAME` for the canonical C++ report. Classification ports print a
confusion matrix. See [migration notes](docs/nn-language-migration.md) and the
[Python](examples/python/nn/README.md) / [R](examples/r/nn/README.md) example docs.

# Binding examples: Bayesian-tuned Iris MLP

Every block below loads the bundled Iris dataset and fits the same native MLP
classifier using \***Petal.Length and Petal.Width only\***, both measured in centimetres.
The three output classes are setosa, versicolor and virginica.

`MLPClassifierSearch` performs a seeded, stratified 90/30/30 split: candidate
networks learn from 90 rows, hidden width is chosen on 30 validation rows, and
30 test rows remain untouched until the end. A Gaussian-process surrogate with
expected improvement follows four random proposals with eight Bayesian proposals,
searching \***2–24 hidden nodes\*** in one tanh hidden layer. Continuous proposals are
rounded to integers; repeated widths reuse a cached fit. The printed history shows
all 12 proposals and which were cached. The objective is validation mean log loss,
not training accuracy or test accuracy.

All other settings stay fixed: 400 SGD epochs, learning rate 0.05, batch size 32,
L2 penalty 0.0001 and seed 42. Predictor standardization is fitted only on the
candidate's training rows. The selected width is then refitted on all 120 development
rows, including new standardization statistics, before the final test score is
computed. Validation loss is the selected candidate's loss before refitting.

Each plot shows the final model's predicted class regions and the 120 development
observations, coloured by their actual species. The 120 × 120 region grid is a
visual approximation of the decision boundary; test points are not overlaid.
This is a small worked example, not a claim that one split finds the globally best
architecture. Edit the visible search controls to explore other budgets or seeds.

C-c C-c runs each block in its `report-*` Nix shell, which supplies the language
runtime and binding. Training, search and SVG rendering use native datamunge.
Images are local build output;
MEP embeds the saved SVG through the block's `file=` option.

## C/C++

```cpp {nix-shell=".#report-cpp", results="output", file="build/iris-mlp-cpp.svg", cmd="c++ -std=c++23 -O2 {file} -o {bin} $(pkg-config --cflags --libs datamunge) -Wl,-rpath,$(pkg-config --variable=libdir datamunge) && {bin}"}
#include <dm/dm.hpp>

int main() {
  dm::mkdir("build");
  const std::unique_ptr<dm::DataFrame> iris(dm::data::iris());
  dm::MLPClassifierSearch fit(*iris, "Species", "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width",
                              2, 24, 4, 8, 400, 42);
  std::cout << fit.summary() << '\n';
  const std::unique_ptr<dm::DataFrame> trials(fit.trials());
  std::cout << trials->to_md(6) << '\n';
  fit.plot_decision_regions().save("build/iris-mlp-cpp.svg");
}
```

## D

```d {nix-shell=".#report-d", results="output", file="build/iris-mlp-d.svg", cmd="ldc2 -I$DATAMUNGED_SOURCE {file} $DATAMUNGED_SOURCE/datamunge.d $DATAMUNGED_SOURCE/datamunge_im.d -of={bin} && {bin}"}
module iris_mlp;
import std.file : exists, mkdirRecurse;
import std.stdio : writeln;
import datamunge;

void main() {
  if (!exists("build")) mkdirRecurse("build");
  auto iris = data_iris();
  auto fit = new MLPClassifierSearch(iris, "Species", "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width",
                                     2, 24, 4, 8, 400, 42);
  writeln(fit.summary());
  auto trials = fit.trials();
  writeln(trials.to_md(6));
  auto regions = fit.plot_decision_regions();
  regions.save("build/iris-mlp-d.svg");
}

## Go

```go {nix-shell=".#report-go", results="output", file="build/iris-mlp-go.svg"}
package main

import (
    "datamunge"
    "datamunge/data"
    "fmt"
    "os"
)

func main() {
    if err := os.MkdirAll("build", 0755); err != nil { panic(err) }
    iris := datamunge.Must(data.Iris())
    defer iris.Close()
    fit := datamunge.Must(datamunge.NewMLPClassifierSearchWithSeed(
        iris, "Species", "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width", 2, 24, 4, 8, 400, 42))
    defer fit.Close()
    fmt.Println(datamunge.Must(fit.Summary()))
    trials := datamunge.Must(fit.Trials())
    defer trials.Close()
    fmt.Println(datamunge.Must(trials.ToMdWithDigits(6)))
    regions := datamunge.Must(fit.PlotDecisionRegions())
    defer regions.Close()
    if err := regions.Save("build/iris-mlp-go.svg"); err != nil { panic(err) }
}
```

## Guile/Scheme

```scheme {nix-shell=".#report-guile", results="output", file="build/iris-mlp-guile.svg"}
(use-modules (oop goops) (datamunge) ((datamunge data) #:select (iris)))
(unless (file-exists? "build") (mkdir "build"))

(define flowers (iris))
(define fit (make <mlp-classifier-search> flowers "Species" "Petal.Length" "Petal.Width"
                  2 24 4 8 400 42))
(display (summary fit)) (newline)
(define history (trials fit))
(display (to-md history 6)) (newline)
(define regions (plot-decision-regions fit))
(save regions "build/iris-mlp-guile.svg")
(for-each close! (list regions history fit flowers))
```

import datamunge.data.Data;

class Main {
  public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {

  }
}

## OCaml

```ocaml {nix-shell=".#report-ocaml", results="output", file="build/iris-mlp-ocaml.svg"}
#use "topfind";;
#require "datamunge";;
open Datamunge;;

let () =
  if not (Sys.file_exists "build") then Sys.mkdir "build" 0o755;
  let iris = Data.iris () in
  let fit = MLPClassifierSearch.create iris "Species" "Petal.Length" "Petal.Width"
      ~min_hidden:2 ~max_hidden:24 ~initial_samples:4 ~iterations:8 ~epochs:400 ~seed:42 in
  print_endline (MLPClassifierSearch.summary fit);
  let trials = MLPClassifierSearch.trials fit in
  print_endline (DataFrame.to_md ~digits:6 trials);
  let regions = MLPClassifierSearch.plot_decision_regions fit in
  RPlot.save regions "build/iris-mlp-ocaml.svg"
```
